children: Premiums on some of BSE Sensex's
put options spiked between 400% to 500% during closing auction on Thursday, as indicative close for India's benchmark stock index briefly dropped to 2.5% lower, as per BSE's website.
The swings coincided with the expiry of Sensex weekly futures and options contracts.

Indian equities have seen sharp moves during the newly launched closing auction session (CAS), particularly on derivatives expiry days, prompting traders to cut positions and increase hedging in one of the world's largest derivatives markets.
Volatility has been particularly high on BSE Sensex contracts compared the Nifty 50 index
given thinner trading volumes on the exchange, analysts said.

"Put sellers will be at loss today due to these sharp moves. We have advised clients to close trades before closing auction begins as it is very difficult to predict what would happen in those fifteen to twenty minutes," said Ratnesh Goyal, head technical and derivatives analyst at Arihant Capital Markets.
The premium for 76,400 points put option of Sensex spiked to 247.05 rupees from 47.35 rupees during CAS.
Similar jumps were seen in several other put contracts as Sensex's indicative close briefly slipped more than 2,100 points within minutes during CAS, indicating a potential drop of 2.5%.
The 30-stock index bounced back and closed 0.55% lower at 76,152.86 points. Meanwhile, Nifty 50

"These kind of moves encourage speculative traders to come in as they may get induced by prospects of jackpot profit, while regular traders are cutting down their positions ahead of the closing auction due to continued volatility," said Rajesh Palviya, senior vice president and head of research at Axis Securities.
